newsitem.title: KENYA: Kenya shilling firms on low importer dlr demand.
newsitem.headline: Kenya shilling firms on low importer dlr demand.

text.p: The Kenyan shilling continued to strengthen against the dollar on Tuesday amid low importer demand for dollars, dealers said.
The Central Bank of Kenya posted a mean shilling average of 55.64 against the dollar from 55.68 on Monday. On the pound, the shilling was posted at 92.94 from 92.75.
Dealers said exporter sales continued to flow into the market amid low demand for hard currencies lending support to the shilling.
"Importers have adopted a wait-and-see attitude in the face of a strengthening shilling," a commercial dealer said.
"Actually, all importers seem to be doing is sniffing around, looking to buy, but they are discouraged by the strengthening shilling," another dealer said.
They said the shilling opened at 55.62/65 levels and traded along thin margins.
"Trading along thin margins shows that people have money. It's just that many importers, mainly oil companies, are speculating, hoping the shilling will go down," one said.
The money market was tight with rates quoted as high as 24 percent from Monday's 20-25 percent levels.
Rates were expected to drop into the teens this week due to a large number of treasury bills due for redemption.
